name: MyCase
tagline: All-in-one case management for small law firms: matters, time and billing, trust accounting, client portal, e-payments.

pricing.basis: per user per month, billed annually
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible surface of MyCase is boring CRUD: matters, contacts, tasks, documents, time entries, invoices. An agent will hand you that in an afternoon and it will look fine. The part it cannot hand you is IOLTA trust accounting that survives a bar audit, card and ACH processing that keeps client funds legally segregated, a client portal your clients will actually trust with privileged material, e-signature, court calendaring rules, and the paper trail your malpractice insurer expects. A solo practitioner who self-hosts their trust ledger on a laptop is not saving money, they are buying a new category of risk. Build the matter tracker if you want, keep the money and the privileged documents somewhere accountable.
coreLoopDIY: A local matter and time tracker: log matters, contacts, notes, billable time entries, and generate PDF invoices, with no trust accounting and no client-facing portal.
requirements: Encrypted disk and real backups if any actual client data touches it
A separate, compliant system for trust accounting and client payments
whatYouLose: Trust and IOLTA accounting with three-way reconciliation, the thing bar associations audit
Integrated card and ACH payments with proper handling of retainers and earned/unearned funds
A client portal for secure messaging and document sharing that clients can log into
E-signature, court rules calendaring, document assembly, and the QuickBooks/Outlook/Google integrations
Someone else's SOC 2 report, uptime guarantees, and liability when the data goes missing
moatNotes: Legal software moats are mostly liability transfer. Firms pay so the audit trail belongs to a vendor with insurance.
whyPeopleStillPay: A small firm is one bad trust reconciliation away from a disciplinary complaint, so the calculation is not features per dollar, it is who is holding the bag. MyCase bundles the ledger, the payment rails, the client portal, and the reporting into one system that opposing counsel, accountants, and the bar all recognise. Migrating years of matters, documents, and billing history out of it is genuinely painful, which is the other half of the moat. Forty dollars a seat is cheap next to an hour of the malpractice defence it quietly avoids.
notes: The matter tracker is a weekend; the trust ledger is not. The moat is compliance liability plus payment rails, and nobody wants their IOLTA reconciliation running on a hobby project.
prompt:
Build a local-only matter and time tracking app for a solo legal practice. This is a private practice management notebook, NOT a trust accounting or payments system.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/practice.db
- Drizzle ORM with migrations checked into the repo
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, no auth, no cloud, no telemetry

Data model:
- contacts: name, role (client, opposing, court, other), email, phone, notes
- matters: title, client contact, practice area, status (open, on hold, closed), opened date, hourly rate, flat fee (nullable), description
- notes: matter id, timestamp, body (markdown)
- tasks: matter id, title, due date, done flag, priority
- timeEntries: matter id, date, minutes, narrative, billable flag, invoiced flag
- expenses: matter id, date, amount cents, description, billable flag
- invoices: matter id, number, issued date, period start/end, subtotal cents, status (draft, sent, paid), plus line items snapshotted at generation time

Features:
- Matter list with filters by status and practice area, and a matter detail page with tabs for notes, tasks, time, expenses, invoices
- Fast time entry: a always-visible form with matter picker, duration in minutes or decimal hours, and narrative
- Running timer that persists across reloads (store start time in the DB)
- Invoice generation: select an uninvoiced date range for a matter, produce a draft, mark entries invoiced, render a printable HTML invoice page styled for A4 that prints to PDF via the browser
- Simple reports: billable hours by matter and by month, unbilled work in progress, realisation rate
- CSV export of every table and a `npm run backup` script that copies the DB file with a timestamp

Explicitly out of scope, do not build stubs for these:
- Trust/IOLTA accounting, retainers, client funds of any kind
- Card or ACH payment processing
- Client portal, client logins, secure messaging
- E-signature, court rules calendaring, e-filing

Include a seed script with two fake matters, a README that states in the first paragraph that this app must not be used to track client funds, and a .env.example with only APP_NAME and DEFAULT_HOURLY_RATE.
